newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thousands of passengers still stranded in Bangkok.
newsitem.headline: Thousands of passengers still stranded in Bangkok.

text.p: Thousands of passengers remained stranded in the Thai capital Bangkok late on Sunday as airlines struggled to clear a backlog of delays caused by an Indian air traffic controllers strike, airline officials said.

The industrial action indefinitely delayed scheduled Friday flights on a number of airlines carrying passengers from Bangkok to Europe, officials said. Other airports in the region, including Singapore and Hong Kong, were similarly affected.
The strike was called off on Saturday and normal flight services have been resumed, officials said.
But around 3,000 passengers remain stuck in Thailand where where a four day public holiday has left airlines struggling to lay on extra flights to clear the backlog, officials said.
Passengers said tempers had flared at Bangkok's Don Muang International airport in the early hours of Sunday morning and security guards were called to protect staff from irate passengers.

"There could have been a riot at the airport last night, they called guards after one man broke a table, no one wants to make decisons, or take responsibility and nobody seems to know anything," said Marc Heinze, from Essen.

"People were banging fists on the desks and shouting ... they called security guards who stood infront of the desks to make sure the passengers couldn't reach the staff," said Roswitha Hullman, also from Essen in Germany.
"People have been treated like dirt ... They told us to come to the airport and then put us all on standby for a flight that was already fully booked," she said.
Most airlines had booked passengers into hotels in the outskirts of Bangkok, hotel managers said.
Thai Airways officials said some extra flights to Europe had been arranged for Sunday night.
In the lounge of one hotel Helen Randolph, from London, hugged her two sons, and said she just hoped their ordeal would end soon.
"One of the children is ill, we are at the end of our holiday, we are nearly out of money and clean clothes," she said.
"We had to spend the first night in the airport where the children were being bitten by mosquitos. We really just want to go home," she said.
